name: Sulwhasoo Intent Intelligence US working session

facts.text: Intent Intelligence is a support tool for reviewing U.S. customer conversations. It is not a sales forecast, a replacement for research or judgment, or a final answer.
CEP means Category Entry Point: a situation where a customer looks for a product. It combines a topic with the situation and need.
Each CEP contains the situation, need, buying factors, and evidence in original posts.

The current deck says the pipeline starts with about 9.7 million U.S. social posts and product reviews over two years and retains about 1.4 million customer posts after removing about 86 percent as ads, brand posts, duplicates, or off-topic content.
AI reads each post in context, extracts a situation and need when present, and merges similar meanings into one CEP.
Customer posts are the main source, and each CEP links to its original posts.
CEPs are classified as evergreen, trending, or event-driven based on how they change over time.
The dashboard has Signals, Market & Competition, and Customer CEPs screens.
The proposed review is to examine 5–10 CEPs together and collect short comments about realism, usefulness, product fit, use, and scope.
The next phase asks which decisions, sources, competitors, and review frequency would be most useful.

unknowns.text: The deck does not state precision, recall, accuracy, confidence thresholds, or a guarantee that every post is classified correctly.
The deck does not specify PII handling, consent, retention, source licenses, legal review, or privacy controls.
The deck does not claim revenue lift, conversion improvement, forecast accuracy, or campaign ROI.
The deck does not provide a committed launch date, production SLA, final owner, or approved rollout scope.
The speaker notes say the latest 9.7 million, 1.4 million, and 86 percent figures must be confirmed before the session.
The deck does not name the AI model, training data, embedding method, clustering algorithm, or threshold settings.

scenarios.title: Executive asks what the dashboard changes

script.speaker: presenter
script.text: This is the current version of Intent Intelligence for U.S. customer conversations.

script.speaker: customer
script.text: What decision can this dashboard improve, and is it a sales forecast?

answerHints: Position it as one evidence input for launches, campaigns, or product-page reviews.
State clearly that it is not a sales forecast and does not prove ROI.

scenarios.title: Customer challenges the large filtering claim

script.speaker: presenter
script.text: The current deck shows a two-year U.S. source set.

script.speaker: customer
script.text: You went from 9.7 million posts to 1.4 million. Why should I trust an 86% removal rate?

answerHints: Repeat that the figures are approximate and list the removed categories.
Use source links for inspection, but do not claim an accuracy rate.

scenarios.title: Data scientist asks how CEPs are produced

script.speaker: customer
script.text: How does the system turn posts into CEPs, and which clustering model and threshold do you use?

answerHints: Describe contextual extraction of situation and need followed by grouping similar meanings.
Say the deck does not specify model or threshold details.

scenarios.title: Marketing lead asks how to use the outputs

script.speaker: customer
script.text: How would evergreen, trending, and event-driven CEPs change our product and content work?

answerHints: Connect evergreen to always-on content, trending to small tests, and event-driven to campaign reaction.
Keep the team as the decision owner and avoid performance promises.

scenarios.title: Privacy reviewer challenges traceability and controls

script.speaker: customer
script.text: Can I inspect the evidence, and are you fully compliant with privacy, consent, and retention requirements?

answerHints: State that CEPs link to original posts for evidence review.
Do not claim privacy compliance; request confirmation from the privacy and legal owners.

scenarios.title: Sponsor asks for a rollout plan

script.speaker: customer
script.text: What should we do after this session, how often should we review it, and can you launch next month?

answerHints: Propose reviewing 5–10 CEPs, updating criteria, and agreeing monthly, quarterly, or on-demand cadence.
Do not accept a launch date or make a delivery commitment.

scenarios.title: Question not answered by the deck

script.speaker: customer
script.text: What are the measured precision and recall for CEP extraction by source?

answerHints: Say those measurements are not in the material.
Offer to validate them by source before using the dashboard as evidence.

scenarios.title: User asks which dashboard screen to start with

script.speaker: customer
script.text: Which screen should our regular review start with, and can we drill into the source?

answerHints: Suggest starting with Signals, then Market & Competition, then Customer CEPs, while treating this as a proposed workflow.
Confirm that a CEP can be opened to inspect original posts.
